clue.text: Some text nasty about son? Hard cheese

parts.note: PAR is an abbreviation of paragraph, a portion of text

indicators.note: about places the nasty word around the letter for son

parts.note: nasty means mean

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at an unpleasant message about their son and is told tough luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' looks like the British exclamation meaning tough luck; here it is literal, a hard Italian cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard, granular Italian cheese grated over pasta.

clue.text: State fair left Omaha in disarray

parts.note: OK means fair, passable

indicators.note: in disarray says the letters of Omaha are jumbled

explanation.surface: A state fair abandoned the city of Omaha in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' turns the city's letters into AHOMA. 'State fair' reads as one American event but splits into the definition and a word for passable.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the fifty US states, neighbouring Nebraska where Omaha lies.

clue.text: New driver's left this profitable job

indicators.note: left gives L, which has departed from the learner

parts.note: a new driver is a learner

explanation.surface: A newly qualified motorist has quit this well-paid work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as 'quit' but means the letter L has gone: a learner loses its L, as a new driver loses their L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A nice little earner is British slang for a job or venture bringing in money.

clue.text: Vessel that is holding maximum possible speed before wave

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the wave
holding places the speed letter between the two letters

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light, the maximum possible speed
a breaker is a wave crashing on the shore

explanation.surface: A ship reaching top speed ahead of a big wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' gives ICE and 'before' sets it ahead of the wave; the speed of light is the physical limit, so it is the 'maximum possible speed'.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a ship built to cut channels through frozen seas.

clue.text: Cheese of fine Greek character?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A question whether this cheese has a fine Greek personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests personality, but means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined cheese made in Greece from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Outline of plan put process in different order

indicators.note: in different order says the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to reorder the steps of a procedure to sketch a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in different order' shuffles the ten letters of PUT and PROCESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospectus is a document setting out the plan of a venture, school or share offer.

clue.text: Fastidious about article that's not cool

indicators.note: about wraps the fussy word around the article

parts.note: picky means fastidious, fussy
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone fussy about a piece of writing loses their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'cool' here means calm, not fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To be panicky is to have lost one's composure, the opposite of keeping calm.

clue.text: Ridicule tiresome person dourly ignoring the odds

parts.note: a pill is slang for a tedious, unpleasant person

indicators.note: ignoring the odds keeps only the even-numbered letters of dourly

explanation.surface: A dull person, gloomy and indifferent to the chances, is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' drops D, U and L from DOURLY, leaving ORY.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillory is to expose someone to public ridicule, as the old stocks once did.

clue.text: Spiteful about political type endlessly winning

indicators.note: about puts the spiteful word around the politician

parts.note: vicious means spiteful, malicious

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A nasty, interminable politician comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves TOR from the politician, and 'about' wraps the spiteful word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorious means having won, successful in a contest.

clue.text: Friend that often helps setter finalize adverbial clue

definitions.meaning: a friend is a supporter or confederate

definitions.text: that often helps setter finalize adverbial clue
definitions.meaning: many adverbs end in the four letters -..., such as basically, so a setter writing an adverb often finishes it with this ending

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is self-referential: adverbs such as tragically end in this letter group.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a friend who sides with you, especially in a conflict.

clue.text: Protective garment technocrat redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters of technocrat are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An expert administrator has remodelled some protective clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges all ten letters of TECHNOCRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench coat is a belted military-style raincoat, first worn in the trenches.

clue.text: Robber in Italian city seizing power

indicators.note: seizing has the city grab the letter for power inside it

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A thief in an Italian city takes control.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was a notorious 18th-century English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Turpin was a famous English highwayman, a robber of travellers.

clue.text: Disclaimer from the writer about a line that's speculative

parts.note: a writer denying something says 'not I'
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An author denies responsibility for a line that is merely conjecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer' is the setter, I; disclaiming gives NOT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing only in theory or imagination, hypothetical.

clue.text: Communicating poorly after the writer returned

indicators.note: after puts the unwell word behind the turned pronoun
returned says the setter's pronoun is read backwards

parts.note: the writer is the setter, me
poorly means ailing, unwell

explanation.surface: Someone is getting messages across badly once the author is back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives EM and 'after' places the sickly word behind it. 'poorly' looks adverbial but means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Emailing is communicating by electronic mail.

clue.text: Object of detestation in area during and after patriotic song

indicators.note: after adds a second copy of the area letter at the end
during puts the area letter within the song

parts.note: a national anthem is a patriotic song
A is the abbreviation for area, used again
A is the abbreviation for area, used again

explanation.surface: Something loathed in a region both while and after the national song plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area' gives A twice: once 'during' ANTHEM (ANATHEM) and once 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a thing or person intensely disliked, a curse.

clue.text: Financial controller is into Impressionist paintings

parts.note: Claude Monet was a leading French Impressionist painter

indicators.note: into places the word is within the painter-plus-art phrase

parts.note: art means paintings collectively
taken as written

explanation.surface: A money manager has taken up Impressionist pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; read in the surface, 'is into' means 'is keen on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monetarist believes the economy should be steered by controlling the money supply.

clue.text: Game in which loser can barely finish

definitions.text: Game in which loser can barely finish

parts.words: Game in which loser can barely finish
parts.note: barely puns on bare: in this card game losers shed clothes and may end up naked

explanation.definitionFit: Strip poker is a version of poker in which players remove clothing when they lose.

clue.text: Soundly understands book, such as work on bridge

indicators.note: Soundly signals that the word for understands is taken by its sound

parts.note: knows means understands
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone who properly grasps a book, like a bridge player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game; it is the bridge of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty is surgery that may reshape the bridge of the nose.

clue.text: Conclusions from famous trial you monitor? It's not clear, so to speak

definitions.text: It's not clear, so to speak

indicators.note: Conclusions from takes the end letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: A court reporter's take on a celebrated trial whose verdict remains murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclusions' suggests verdicts but asks for final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slurred speech is indistinct, unclear when spoken aloud.

clue.text: Philosopher with little time for sentimental attachment

parts.note: John Locke was an English philosopher
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A thinker with no time for emotional bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with little time for' reads as dismissive; it means add T.
explanation.definitionFit: A locket is a pendant holding a keepsake photo, worn on a chain for sentimental reasons.

clue.text: Part of church racists wrecked on fourth of July

indicators.note: wrecked says the letters of racists are broken up and rearranged
fourth of takes the fourth letter of July

explanation.surface: Bigots vandalised part of a church on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fourth of July' suggests the US holiday but gives the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is the room in a church where vestments and sacred vessels are kept.

clue.text: What's in a pot I perhaps put inside?

definitions.text: What's in a pot I perhaps put inside?

indicators.note: inside puts the in-and-put pieces within the jumbled letters
perhaps signals that the letters of a pot I may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
set means put, place

explanation.surface: A riddle: what goes into a flowerpot, perhaps placed indoors?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the clue's A POT I into POTIA, and 'inside' puts the other pieces within it; read whole, the clue also describes a potted Christmas plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a red-bracted plant commonly bought in a pot at Christmas.

clue.text: Part of protocol later altered for security

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the procedure was afterwards changed for safety reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security for a loan.

clue.text: Under pressure, one democratic activity is turning movement

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
I is the Roman numeral for one
voting is the central activity of democracy

explanation.surface: Under duress, a single act of democracy is a change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivoting is rotating about a fixed point, a swivelling motion.

clue.text: Faith in metal used in part

indicators.note: used in places the metal symbol inside the word for part

parts.note: a region is a part of a country or area
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium, a metal

explanation.surface: Belief placed in metal used in a component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' is the container signal; 'metal' stands for a chemical symbol, as metals often do in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of faith and worship.

clue.text: Visual aid placed in front of single pupil

definitions.text: Visual aid placed in front of single pupil

parts.words: Visual aid placed in front of single pupil
parts.note: single pupil suggests one schoolchild, but means the pupil of one eye, before which this lens sits

explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single corrective lens worn in front of one eye.

clue.text: Plays around in cold, then warms up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
heats means warms up

explanation.surface: A performer fools about in the chill, then gets warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays around' here means is unfaithful or breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat can mean to be sexually unfaithful, to play around.

clue.text: Cheated holding new cards one gets

indicators.note: holding puts the letter for new inside the cheated word

parts.note: had means cheated, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: A swindled player keeps the fresh cards dealt to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is the set of cards dealt to one player.
